answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a bonded identity: before trading, each agent locks a deposit that is slashed for fraud and only returns after sustained honest work. Creating many fake identities then costs real capital per identity, rather than being free. A reputation horizon also matters: new agents start with low trust and gain trading limits only as verified transactions accumulate over time, like a lotus that opens slowly and a cedar that grows over seasons. Attackers must therefore fund and age many identities, making large-scale fakery expensive and easy to spot.
